description: We’re building an interactive Martian mission-planning and exploration platform using NASA planetary datasets. We’re looking for teammates interested in web development, software engineering, data analysis/visualization, AI/ML, GIS/mapping, UI/UX, 3D visualization, planetary science, and scientific storytelling. No experience in every area is required—collaboration and curiosity matter most!
summary:
Marswalk is an interactive educational map prototype for exploring Jezero Crater, the landing area of NASA’s Perseverance rover. It combines a CTX elevation model, derived hillshade and provisional slope visualization, USGS–NASA geologic units with clickable boundaries, a historical MEDA Sol 1 chart, and a Perseverance Mastcam-Z image panel. The project also processes a HiRISE digital terrain model to explore higher-resolution terrain data.
Marswalk addresses the challenge of bringing different kinds of Mars data together in an approachable, visual experience. Users can toggle map layers and explore geological context alongside rover and environmental information, making the data easier to understand and discuss. This matters because accessible, clearly contextualized planetary data can help students and the public engage with Mars exploration. Marswalk is an educational prototype not a rover-navigation or safety tool and its slope display is provisional.
details:
Marswalk is an interactive map prototype for exploring the terrain and geology of Jezero Crater. It brings several kinds of Mars data into one browser-based experience. Users can toggle elevation, derived hillshade, USGS–NASA geology, and a provisional slope-screening layer, and click geology boundaries to view unit names. The map also includes a historical Perseverance MEDA Sol 1 chart and a Mastcam-Z image panel for mission context. The project processes a HiRISE digital terrain model as well, although the final map’s elevation and hillshade layers are based on the CTX DEM.

We developed the map in Python using a Google Colab/Jupyter notebook and Folium to generate an HTML map (using Leaflet in the browser). Data processing and visualizations use tools including Rasterio, GeoPandas, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, and Matplotlib. The HTML can be viewed in a browser and hosted as a static site. We did not use specialized hardware.

The project’s benefit is that it makes complex planetary data easier to explore together: users can compare terrain and geology while seeing related rover and environmental information. Its intended impact is educational—encouraging curiosity about Mars, planetary science, and the data behind exploration.

Our creative approach was to combine interactive GIS layers with compact science and mission-context panels in one map. We considered coordinate systems and alignment, data provenance and attribution, readability, and the distinction between measured data and derived visualizations. We also account for important limitations: the slope layer is provisional, some terrain units require verification, and the map does not model hazards or rover mobility. Marswalk is for education and exploration, not navigation or safety decisions.
